item.text: I’m looking for the next structural improvement rather than cosmetic churn. The remaining duplication is in traversal: there are three nearly identical recursive methods plus a `switch` that only exists to pick one of them.
I’m consolidating traversal policy into the enum itself now. That removes the tree-level `switch` and the three near-identical recursive methods, so order semantics live in one place.
The traversal refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running the demo now to confirm the enum-driven traversal preserved behavior.
I’ve verified the output stayed stable. I’m pulling line references now so the summary can point at the new enum-driven traversal design instead of describing it abstractly.

Further refactored traversal in [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:8) so traversal order is now defined by the `TraversalOrder` enum itself instead of by tree-level control flow.

The main change is that each enum constant now carries its visit sequence ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:8)), and `forEach(...)` just delegates to `order.traverse(...)` ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:102)). That let me remove the traversal `switch` and the separate preorder/inorder/postorder recursive methods, replacing them with one generic traversal engine at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:177). The result is that traversal behavior is centralized where the order concept already lives.

Verification: `javac AVLTree.java AVLTreeDemo.java` succeeded, and `java AVLTreeDemo` still prints `30 20 10 25 40 50`.
